(B) Projection check (result 2e209b30..., update_id 20, time_s 0.2): reduced-vs-full same-time tip difference 0.004397505013137543 m, velocity difference 0.021396155330638593 m/s; this is a model/projection mismatch, not a tip-error or optimizer hypothesis. (C) The decisive new result, the single-factor saved_state_comparison (result abd59b6a..., update_id 20, feasible_return.budget_s 15 vs 30, common constant-previous-input seed, budget_effect_isolated true, feasible_return_budget_triggered true in both arms): the SELECTED plan is the initial 0.2 N seed in BOTH arms (objective total 1697.0857483254906, feasible at scaled_violation 2.927345865710862e-14, iteration 0, stop_reason budget_best_feasible). The 15 s arm ran 18 iterations in 15.583082799974363 s and reached best lower-objective-infeasible objective 22.306038779879355 at scaled_violation 0.042687068291809294 and least-infeasible-noninitialization 27.527303922251033 at scaled_violation 0.013844345207850856; the 30 s arm ran 37 iterations in 30.685413100000005 s and reached 18.37680755669539 at scaled_violation 0.0009537607210136773 and 18.674613911154182 at scaled_violation 0.0007145889734799793. So extending the feasible-return budget from 15 to 30 s lowered the best candidate objective (22.31 -> 18.38) and increased iterations (18 -> 37), but every improved non-seed candidate remained numerically infeasible at the 1e-5 threshold (best 9.54e-4, two orders above), leaving the feasible 0.2 N seed as the best feasible incumbent and the selected/applied plan. Therefore the pure "budget/early-stop" account of initialization dominance at update_id 20 is not supported: the binding obstacle is the numerical infeasibility of improved plans within the allowed 30 s CPU, not merely insufficient return time, and the initialization-dominated behavior is a plan-selection outcome (feasible seed retained) distinct from exception fallback, optimizer progress (objective did fall), projection disagreement, and task acceptance. No unique or dominant cause, and no model/optimizer/weight superiority, is claimed; because the isolated factor changed neither the selected plan nor its feasibility, no closed-loop revision against the imported baseline is warranted and no new simulation is run. Recommendation-only procedure: any future revision must first exhibit a factor that makes improved non-seed plans numerically feasible at 1e-5; only then is a one-factor closed-loop revision justified. (D) My own redundant re-run of this same pair returned only an engineering failure (evidence_reference 5def7eebcf14ee45ad87fc00c8bbd6bac32d91d9fdf9bab65060cc49314468e4: PAIRED_INTERFACE_FAILURE: OPERATION_TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED_AFTER_RETURN, nlp_solves 0), which is an engineering result and not a scientific one.

hypothesis: The reach-hold failure with initialization-dominated plan selection at update_id 20 is not explained by the feasible-return time budget alone: the returned single-factor comparison shows that doubling feasible_return.budget_s from 15 to 30 s (18 -> 37 iterations) lowers the best candidate objective from 22.306038779879355 to 18.37680755669539 but leaves every improved non-seed candidate numerically infeasible at 1e-5 (best scaled_violation 0.0009537607210136773), so the numerically feasible 0.2 N seed remains the selected and applied plan in both arms. The binding obstacle at this state is the numerical infeasibility of improved plans under the fixed constraints, not insufficient return time or exception fallback.
limitations: The comparison uses a new common constant-previous-input seed with regenerated states, not a historical warm replay; historical complete warm starts, raw plan vectors, rejected iterates, scalar objectives and iteration counts were not recorded.

The 30 s feasible-return budget coincides with the fixed 30 s CPU cap, so run length and budget are not fully separable even though the termination reports budget_effect_isolated true and no other limit increased.

Results are single execution, single state (update_id 20) and single seed; they are not generalizable to all states, weights, or the full 0.35 s trajectory, and no unique or dominant cause is established.
Numerical feasibility and candidate-objective progress do not imply task acceptance or closed-loop improvement; the rad/m curvature and rate residuals are not metre tip errors.
The same controller did escape the seed at effective_horizon 5 (relative_seed_improvement) and converge at horizon 4 and below, so the result here does not characterize all updates.
revision_or_stop_rule: STOP now: no further local pairs, ceiling changes, closed-loop revision or independent replay are requested. weakening_observation: Weakening facts (reported, not suppressed): the selected plan was identical in both budget arms, so the budget-dominance hypothesis is not supported; the improvement in candidate objective (22.31 -> 18.38) came with candidates still infeasible at 1e-5, the comparison is one state and one synthetic seed, and the 30 s budget coincides with the fixed 30 s CPU cap.
